To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the children’s socialization into perspective-taking is accomplished through triadic conflict mediation, and that the teachers’ mediation is guided by the Swedish preschools’ pedagogical values of democratic values of equality and agency.

the teachers' triadic conflict mediation is a form of socialization into perspective-taking, and that the teachers' discursive practices are linked to wider societal values of Swedish preschools, and Swedish society, including democratic values of equality and agency, and individualism and solidarity.

preschool teachers in Sweden socialize children into triadic conflict mediation by encouraging and directing children to convey their perspective to the other party and requesting the other children to take the perspective of the other party.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which preschools socialize children to the interactional and linguistic competences needed in conflict situations.

the social and interactional processes through which children are socialized into the discursive and interactional practices of perspective taking, which are necessary for managing conflict in preschool settings.
the socialization of preschool children into the discursive and interactional practices of perspective taking and conflict mediation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the teachers' ways of conflict mediation socialized children into the perspective taking necessary for resolving conflicts in ways that are in accordance with the Swedish preschool pedagogy of democratic values of equality and individualism, and the wider Swedish society.

the teachers' mediation practices socialized children into the perspective taking and interactional competence necessary for managing conflicts in a way that was consistent with the wider societal norms of democratic values.

triadic conflict mediation is a socialization practice that is used by teachers to socialize young children into the perspective taking and interactional competences needed to manage conflict situations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preschool teachers in our study used triadic interactions to socialize young children to conflict resolution and perspective taking.

this paper is a video ethnographic language socialization analysis of the discursive practices of triadic conflict mediation in Swedish preschools and how these discursive practices socialized children into the interactional skills necessary for conflict management and perspective taking.
this study contributes with empirical knowledge about how children’s social and emotional skills are fostered in the early years.
The main takeaway from our work is that

children’s socialization into perspective-taking is not only a matter of the children’s own social and linguistic competencies, but also a matter of the social practices and norms in which they are embedded, as well as a matter of their social and physical environments.
the socialization of young children into perspective taking is a complex and multifaceted process.
preschool teachers in Sweden are socializing children to perspective taking in ways that are consistent with democratic values of equality and agency.
